key_insight: A retrieval-augmented foundation model trained on large-scale matched molecular pair transformations can generate diverse, controllable analogs that reproduce medicinal chemistry intuition by operating in a variable-to-variable edit space.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between whole-molecule generative models (which lack fine-grained edit control) and small, restricted MMP learners by enabling scalable, controllable MMP-style transformations from large data.
method: Formulate analog design as a variable-to-variable mapping between molecular fragments/contexts (matched molecular pairs) rather than whole-molecule generation.
Pretrain a foundation model on a large corpus of matched molecular pair transformations (MMPTs) to learn generic edit patterns and produce diverse outputs conditioned on an input variable.
Augment generation with a retrieval mechanism that supplies similar historical transformations or context snippets to improve edit relevance, controllability, and sample efficiency.
impact: Provides a scalable, interpretable tool for medicinal chemistry-aware molecular design that improves controllability of edits and accelerates analog exploration, making it practical to integrate large pre-trained models into drug discovery workflows.
visual_elements: Schematic: variable-to-variable mapping showing input fragment → edit region → generated analogs
Architecture diagram: retrieval-augmented pipeline (query → retrieve relevant MMPT examples → foundation model → candidate outputs)
Before/after examples: a few concrete matched molecular pair edits with chemist-style annotations (e.g., potency, lipophilicity changes)
Performance chart: comparisons of diversity, edit accuracy, and controllability vs baseline whole-molecule and small MMP models
paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Foundation Models for Matched Molecular Pair Transformations to Recapitulate Medicinal Chemistry Intuition
paper_authors: Bo Pan, Peter Zhiping Zhang, Hao-Wei Pang, Alex Zhu, Xiang Yu
